\section[\texorpdfstring{\te{కమ్మని} (kammani)}{కమ్మని (kammani)}]{\te{కమ్మని} (kammani) — delicious, tasty}

\label{lesson:TE-C179-kammani}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for a condition, then the Telugu for an excuse.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{కమ్మని}}
\textbf{\te{కమ్మని}} — \emph{kammani} — \textquotedblleft{}delicious, tasty\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\te{కమ్మని}} (\emph{kammani}) is native Dravidian. DEDR 1247 lists \emph{kammani}, \textquotedblleft{}delicious, sweet\textquotedblright{}, beside \emph{kampu}, \textquotedblleft{}smell\textquotedblright{}, with Kannada \emph{kamma}, \textquotedblleft{}fragrance\textquotedblright{}. DEDR compares Hindi \emph{gamak}, \textquotedblleft{}fragrance\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kammani}, once more

\end{itemize}

\end{cousinweb}
